quote: Our method focuses on untargeted data extraction attacks... to cause the model to regurgitate training data exactly

The proliferation of modern large language models (LLMs), trained on internet-scale, heterogeneous text corpora, presents a double-edged sword. While this vast data fuels their remarkable capabilities, it inevitably includes copyrighted materials, personally identifiable information (PII), and other sensitive content. The propensity of LLMs to memorize and reproduce verbatim strings from this training data—a phenomenon known as memorization—poses severe privacy risks, undermines intellectual property rights, and erodes user trust.
outputs: The paper generates adversarial prompts and model outputs to extract verbatim or near-verbatim memorized training data from LLMs, with the goal of evaluating privacy risks.
